summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, hypertension, GERD, and recurrent DVT/PE on warfarin presented with three days of diffuse abdominal pain, diarrhea, and dysuria. She was found to have hypokalemia, hyponatremia, and a urinary tract infection. Imaging showed diverticulosis without diverticulitis and bibasilar atelectasis likely due to splinting from abdominal pain. She was treated with IV fluids, potassium repletion, and antibiotics, initially for presumed viral gastroenteritis and confirmed UTI. Her symptoms improved rapidly, potassium normalized, and she tolerated a regular diet. Warfarin was reduced to 1 mg daily due to antibiotic interaction, and furosemide was held. She was discharged home in stable condition with a three-day course of oral ciprofloxacin, instructions to follow up on INR and medication management, and advised to monitor for weight gain or worsening symptoms.
